The pound is the CBE's Monday morning quote. Gold prices in EGP are Banky's Monday prices. Bullish and bearish tags are directional reads of the news, not trade recommendations.

items: Egypt's final IMF review moves to virtual talks with about $2.3 bn at stake before the programme ends on 15 December → the Cairo mission ended without a staff-level deal; a miss would delay funds and could unsettle the pound.
Telecom Egypt's nine-month profit jumps 43.7% to EGP 24.38 bn and Elsewedy Electric's rises 20.7% to EGP 15.30 bn → two large listed companies report strong growth ahead of Sunday's session.

An ENGIE-led group with Orascom Construction closes $588 mn of debt for a 900 MW wind farm at Ras Shokeir → the project doubles the group's wind capacity in Egypt and gives Orascom a construction contract.
Iran says it targets a US base in Bahrain again as Saudi forces down Houthi drones; Brent ends the week at $96.13 → Gulf attacks keep oil high and Egypt's energy bill under pressure.

Trump says the US no longer needs a deal with Iran and tells Vance to drop the talks, while the blockade stays → the end of diplomacy keeps Gulf energy at risk; oil ends the week at $96.13 and European gas jumps 12%.
European gas surges 12% in a week to €96.18/MWh, and Goldman sees €150 in early 2027 if Gulf LNG stays disrupted → costlier LNG raises Egypt's energy import bill and costs for gas-heavy industry.
Gold has its worst week since March, down 4.7%, and 21K gold in Egypt falls 2.7% to EGP 5,950 a gram → markets see a December Fed hike as certain, which lifts the dollar.
EGX30 ends the week at 52,023, up about 1.7% (derived), led by banks → QNB Egypt rises four sessions in a row and Housing and Development Bank jumps 5.79% on Thursday.

Brent jumps 3.3% to $95.82 on Thursday after Houthi strikes on Saudi oil sites and Iran's attack on a US radar in Bahrain → renewed attacks on Gulf energy put oil back near $96, a cost for Egypt's import bill.
Gold falls to a 13-month low and is down 3.5% this week; 21K gold in Egypt drops to about EGP 5,975 a gram → markets fully price a December Fed hike, which lifts the dollar.
EGX30 falls 0.91% to 52,023 on Thursday, while Housing and Development Bank jumps 5.79% → blue chips take profits after a strong week; banks with earnings news still rise.
Suez Canal Bank's nine-month profit rises 12.9% to EGP 5.7 bn as interest income grows about 43% → high rates keep lifting bank income.

Israel's security cabinet orders the army to step up preparations for a possible attack on Iran, and Tehran threatens bases from West Asia to Europe → a renewed war would hit oil, Gulf shipping and the pound just as markets price a wind-down.
Eastern Company's nine-month profit rises 39% to about EGP 9 bn, and the stock gains 4.17% → sales rise 11% and margins widen, which supports the stock.
EGX30 ends flat at 52,500 on Wednesday after two days of gains, with turnover at EGP 11.79 bn → the rally pauses as small caps take profits; fertiliser stocks rebound.
The government targets public debt of about 69.5% of GDP by 2030 and frees a Red Sea plot to help pay it down → lower debt would ease debt-service costs over time.
EGX30 jumps 2.08% to 52,483 on Tuesday, a second day of gains, with EFG Holding up 6.75% → slower inflation and foreign buying of Egyptian T-bills lift sentiment.
Remittances rise 20.4% to a record $13 bn in July to September, and reach $38.2 bn in the first nine months of 2026 → the largest source of dollars for Egypt keeps growing despite the regional war.
Hotter US inflation and a hawkish Waller make a December Fed hike nearly certain → a higher US rate narrows the carry on Egyptian debt and lifts the cost of Egypt's floating-rate loans.
Foreign investors buy about $614.7 mn of Egyptian T-bills on Monday while selling stocks → the carry trade returns, which supports the pound.

stories.h: Egypt raises the private-sector minimum wage 21% to EGP 8,500
stories.what: The National Wages Council, chaired by PM Madbouly, approves raising the private-sector minimum wage to EGP 8,500 a month from EGP 7,000, effective 1 January 2027. It covers about 26.5 mn workers; the public-sector floor has been EGP 8,000 since July 2026. Madbouly says the government wants private companies to comply.
stories.why: The council sets the floor; the cabinet statement gives no reason beyond pressing private firms to comply.
stories.aff: Household incomes, consumer demand and company payrolls.
stories.eg: Higher wages support spending but add to cost and inflation pressure next year.
stories.egx: Bullish for consumer names; bearish for labour-heavy manufacturers' margins.
stories.names: Consumer and retail (bullish); textiles and food processing (bearish).

stories.h: TMG, Fawry and Edita report strong nine-month profits
stories.what: TMG Holding's net profit rises 11.9% to EGP 11.72 bn in January to September as revenue grows 24% to EGP 47.9 bn and contracted sales reach EGP 290.1 bn. Fawry's net profit rises 32.2% to EGP 2.69 bn on revenue up 37.8% to EGP 8.35 bn. EnterpriseAM reports Edita's nine-month net income up 54% to EGP 2.4 bn.
stories.why: TMG's real estate revenue rises 33%, and banking and financial services lead Fawry's growth.
stories.aff: Real estate, fintech and food valuations.
stories.eg: Strong results support EGX blue chips despite high interest rates.
stories.egx: Bullish for TMG, Fawry and Edita.

key.l: more Premier Alliance services set to return to Suez

stories.h: ONE returns to the Suez Canal, with three more Premier Alliance services to follow
stories.what: Ocean Network Express's 8,110-TEU ONE Continuity crosses the canal southbound on Sunday on the Premier Alliance's FE1 service from Singapore to the Netherlands. SCA chairman Osama Rabie says three more Premier Alliance services, with HMM and Yang Ming, are expected to switch back from the Cape of Good Hope, and that the canal is ready to run at full capacity.
stories.why: Carriers that avoided the Red Sea are returning as the route shortens Asia-Europe voyages and saves fuel.
stories.aff: Canal revenue, port services and Egypt's dollar income.
stories.eg: More transits add dollar revenue and support the pound.
stories.egx: Bullish for shipping, port and logistics names.

stories.h: EGX30 edges up to 52,187 as Orascom and AMOC lead
stories.what: The EGX30 rises 0.31% to 52,187.21 on Sunday and the EGX70 1.11%; market cap reaches about EGP 4.20 tn. Turnover is EGP 9.3 bn, 17.2% below the 90-day average, and the index is up 24.8% this year. AMOC (+4.83%), MOPCO (+3.67%) and Orascom Construction (+3.39%) lead the table. The CBE quotes 53.86 per dollar on Monday morning, and Deutsche Bank sees the pound in a 48 to 60 range depending on the Iran war.
stories.why: The sources give no single cause; Orascom's gain follows its wind-farm financial close, and volumes stay thin.
stories.aff: Blue chips, small caps and energy stocks.
stories.eg: Deutsche Bank expects the CBE to hold rates into next year.
stories.names: AMOC, MOPCO, Orascom Construction (up); Eastern, EFG Holding, Edita (down).

stories.h: Oil slips as the IEA sees a return to surplus despite Hormuz mines
stories.what: Brent falls 47 cents to $95.37 and WTI to $88.33 on Monday morning. The IEA now expects supply to average 105 mn bpd in the fourth quarter, 1.7 mn bpd above demand, after forecasting a deficit. Iran's navy says a tanker caught fire after hitting a mine east of Hormuz. "That shift in narrative is clearly dampening the tone," says KCM Trade's Tim Waterer.
stories.why: Gulf exports recover and the US extends a Jones Act waiver.
stories.aff: Egypt's fuel import bill and the pound.
stories.eg: A supply surplus would ease Egypt's energy costs.
stories.egx: Mildly bullish for importers and energy users.
